name: Teeth Consistency
description: Inspects dental structure geometry, specular reflectance, and inter-tooth boundary precision to identify the characteristically blurred or merged teeth rendered by face generation networks.
mechanism:
This method analyzes teeth rendering and consistency for deepfake detection:

1. **Teeth Detection & Segmentation**: When the mouth is open during speech or smiling, visible teeth are detected and segmented. Individual teeth boundaries, alignment, and arrangement are analyzed per frame.

2. **Dental Anatomy Verification**: The method checks dental anatomy: (a) correct tooth count for visible region, (b) proper tooth shapes (incisors, canines, premolars with distinct morphology), (c) realistic tooth size and spacing, (d) gum line contour. AI generators often produce blurred, merged, or anatomically incorrect teeth — too many, too few, or with impossible shapes.

3. **Teeth Texture & Color**: Real teeth show characteristic features: translucency at the incisal edge, varying color (slightly yellow body, whiter enamel surface), surface texture (microlines, stain patterns). The method evaluates teeth rendering quality. Generated teeth are often unrealistically white, uniformly colored, or lacking surface detail.

4. **Temporal Teeth Stability**: Teeth structure is completely rigid — tooth positions, sizes, and arrangement cannot change between frames. The method tracks teeth geometry frame-to-frame. Changes in visible tooth arrangement (teeth appearing/disappearing, changing shape) indicate AI generation where teeth are rendered independently per frame.

5. **Teeth-Lip Interaction**: During speech, lips interact with teeth in specific ways — upper teeth visible during /f/ and /v/ sounds, teeth edges visible during particular articulations. The method checks teeth-lip coordination. Deepfakes may show teeth visibility that doesn't correlate with the spoken phonemes.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through teeth consistency analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
Matern, F. et al. (2019). Exploiting Visual Artifacts to Expose Deepfakes. WACVW.
